'''Zorya Yakovlevna Shapiro''' ({{langx|ru|Зоря Яковлевна Шапиро}}; 7 December 1914 – 4 July 2013) was a Soviet mathematician, educator and translator. She is known for her contributions to representation theory and functional analysis in her collaboration with [[Israel Gelfand]], and the Shapiro-Lobatinski condition in elliptical boundary value problems.

==Life==
Zorya Shapiro attended the [[MSU Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics|Moscow State University Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics]] from where she received her undergraduate and doctoral degrees by 1938.<ref name=tikhomirov>{{cite journal|journal=Семь Исскуств |url=http://7iskusstv.com/2010/Nomer11/Tikhomirov1.php|title=Прогулки с И.М. Гельфандом|author=Vladimir Tikhomirov|number=12|year=2010|volume=11}}</ref> She was active in the military department of the university, especially in aviation, learning to fly and land aeroplanes.<ref>{{cite book|title=Ровесники Октября|author=Vladimir Tikhomirov|page=6|isbn= 9785040175239|publisher=Litres|year=2011}}</ref>

She started her teaching career at the Faculty, shortly after Zoya Kishkina (1917–1989) and Natalya Eisenstadt (1912–1985), and very quickly became recognized for her courses in analysis.<ref name=tikhomirov/>

Shapiro married [[Israel Gelfand]] in 1942. They had 3 sons, one of whom died in childhood.<ref>{{cite news|newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/obituaries/science-obituaries/6440484/Israel-Gelfand.html|title=Israel Gelfand|date=26 October 2009|accessdate=28 October 2018}}</ref> Shapiro and Gelfand later divorced.<ref>{{cite news|newspaper=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]]|url=https://www.smh.com.au/world/mathematics-genius-had-it-all-figured-out-20091101-hrkd.html|title=Mathematics genius had it all figured out|author=Thomas Maugh|date=2 November 2009|accessdate=28 October 2018}}</ref>

In the 1980s, Shapiro lived in the same house as [[Akiva Yaglom]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ecommons.cornell.edu/bitstream/handle/1813/17258/Yaglom_12-2-1988_transcript.pdf;jsessionid=F678F4A59CF1136677B34B95C958C1A9?sequence=5|title=Akiva M. Yaglom, Dec. 2, 1988; Part 2|accessdate=28 October 2018}}</ref> In 1991 Shapiro moved to [[River Forest, Illinois]] to live with her younger son. She died there on 4 July 2013.

==Career==
Shapiro published several works on [[representation theory]]. A contribution (with Gelfand) in integral geometry was to find inversion formulae for the reconstruction of the value of a function on a manifold in terms of integrals over a family of submanifolds, a result with applicability in [[non-linear differential equations]], [[tomography]], multi-dimensional [[complex analysis]] and other domains.<ref>{{cite journal|journal=An International Conference on "The Unity of Mathematics"|url=http://www.math.harvard.edu/conferences/unityofmath_2003/talks/kazhdan-talk.pdf|author=[[David Kazhdan]]|year=2003|title=Works of I. Gelfand on the theory of representations|page=5|archive-date=2009-11-13|access-date=2018-10-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091113175957/http://www.math.harvard.edu/conferences/unityofmath_2003/talks/kazhdan-talk.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> Another work was on the representations of rotation groups of 3-dimensional spaces.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia|encyclopedia=Колмогоров в воспоминаниях учеников|author=A.A. Yushkevich|title=Колмогоров на моем пути в математику |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=iVfpCgAAQBAJ&pg=PA425|date=5 September 2017|isbn=978-5-457-91890-0|page=425}}</ref>

Shapiro is best known for her elucidation of the conditions for well-defined solutions to the elliptical boundary value problem on [[Sobolev spaces]].<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1112/S1461157000001285|title=The Shapiro–Lopatinskij Condition for Elliptic Boundary Value Problems|author1=Katsiaryna Krupchyk|author2=Jukka Tuomela|journal=LMS Journal of Computation and Mathematics|volume=9|number=|year=2006|pages=287–329|doi-access=free}}</ref>
